title: Server job-execution tests: patch os.name, not sys.platform, to get past the Windows job-backend guard
answers: Server startup tests fail only on Windows with 'MLflow job backend does not support Windows system' instead of the expected rollup validation error
How do I make a test of _run_server pass the job-backend check when job execution or trace rollups are enabled?
Why does mock.patch('sys.platform') not change the behavior of the job executor requirement check?
Where is the Windows rejection for the MLflow job backend implemented?
body:
Path: Server startup in mlflow/server/__init__.py (_run_server) calls validate_executor_config() when job execution is enabled, which reaches LocalJobExecutor.check_requirements in mlflow/server/jobs/local_executor.py; that is where the job backend refuses Windows. Tests in tests/server/test_init.py that enable job execution or trace rollups go through this path.
Rule: To get past the Windows check in a test, patch `os.name` (e.g. mock.patch("os.name", "posix")), because LocalJobExecutor.check_requirements tests `os.name == "nt"`. Patching `sys.platform` with return_value=... does nothing for this guard and is the wrong form for replacing a plain attribute. Keep mocking mlflow.server.jobs.utils._check_requirements alongside it, since that is what the other tests rely on.
Symptom: On Windows CI the startup tests raised 'MLflow job backend does not support Windows system.' before reaching the trace rollup validation, so pytest.raises(match=...) failed with a regex mismatch. On Linux and macOS the same tests passed because os.name was already 'posix', which hid the bug.
Constraints: Only needed for tests that enable job execution and reach validate_executor_config. Tests that do not enable job execution never reach this guard and should not be changed. If a test's own mock raises before the guard (for example a side_effect on _check_requirements), no os.name patch is needed.
applies: Tests under tests/server/ that exercise _run_server with job execution or trace rollups enabled, especially on Windows CI shards.
says: Server startup test suite fails on Windows machines when testing background job execution.
Windows test builds fail with unsupported operating system errors when trace rollups are enabled.
Allow server validation tests to run on Windows without being blocked by backend platform checks.
Background job backend checks prevent trace rollup verification tests from passing on Windows.
Server startup verification crashes on Windows runners before reaching expected schedule validation errors.
search: In tests under tests/server/ that exercise _run_server with job execution or trace rollups enabled, patch os.name to 'posix' rather than patching sys.platform to bypass the Windows platform check. LocalJobExecutor.check_requirements in mlflow/server/jobs/local_executor.py checks os.name == 'nt' during validate_executor_config, so mocking sys.platform fails to prevent the Windows rejection error. Tests such as test_run_server_rejects_invalid_enabled_rollup_schedule and test_run_server_passes_public_store_config_to_job_runner must also continue mocking mlflow.server.jobs.utils._check_requirements. This patch is only required for tests reaching validate_executor_config with job execution enabled, and can be omitted if a mock raises before reaching the guard.
